title: Users, Groups, and Ownership
intro: Services should run as dedicated, unprivileged users that own exactly the files they need — no more. Let's set that up properly for a new app.

steps.prompt: Check who you are and which groups you belong to.
steps.explanation: You're 'deploy', a member of sudo (can run admin commands) and docker (can control Docker).
steps.why: Membership in the docker group is effectively root access — anyone who can run 'docker run -v /:/host' can read and modify the entire host filesystem. Worth knowing exactly who has it.

steps.prompt: Create a system user called 'appsvc' with no login shell, to run the service.
steps.explanation: -r creates a system account; -s /usr/sbin/nologin means nobody can SSH in or get a shell as this user.
steps.why: A service account that can't log in can't be used for interactive access if its credentials ever leak. It exists purely to own files and run one process.

steps.prompt: Give appsvc ownership of the app directory /opt/myapp and everything inside it.
steps.explanation: -R applies recursively to every file and subdirectory.
steps.why: The most common cause of 'Permission denied' after a deploy is files copied in as root (or your own user) that the service account then can't read or write. Fixing ownership is usually the right fix — not chmod 777.

steps.prompt: Make the config file readable only by its owner — it contains a database password.
steps.explanation: 600 = owner read+write (6), group nothing (0), others nothing (0).
steps.why: Octal is worth learning: each digit is read(4)+write(2)+execute(1) for owner/group/others. 600 for secrets, 644 for normal files, 755 for executables and directories covers most real cases.

steps.prompt: Add your 'deploy' user to the 'appsvc' group so you can read the app's logs without sudo.
steps.fake_output: (no output — success; takes effect on next login)
steps.explanation: -aG APPENDS the group to the user's existing groups.
steps.why: Forgetting the -a is a genuinely dangerous mistake: 'usermod -G appsvc deploy' REPLACES all of deploy's groups with just appsvc — silently removing sudo and docker access. Always -aG.

steps.prompt: Verify the permissions and ownership on the config file.
steps.why: Always verify after changing permissions — especially recursive ones, where a typo in the path can change far more than you intended.
